headline: Tech enters November de-grossed but not capitulated: MRVL-LITE is now official (LITE favoured, MRVL questioned), GOOGL is the sentiment laggard, and desks call AMZN/NVDA the safer AI longs into AMD and AAPL prints.
market_read: Desks spent the weekend tallying the worst tech month since Sep-22. Jefferies (1 Nov) had October as its largest net-sell tech month in more than 5 years, and UBS PB (2 Nov) calls last week the 3rd-largest de-gross of the year, concentrated in hyperscalers, with gross still elevated as shorts were added. The near-term call is split: UBS strategy expects ~$100bn of Risk Control selling today before systematic flows fade, while JPM Market Intel (2 Nov) stays Tactically Bullish and JPM Positioning Intel only NEUTRAL. On names, the MRVL-LITE all-stock deal ($115bn EV, 4.5x ratio) is confirmed with a strong LITE FQ2 guide, UBS (1 Nov) ranks the Mag 7 MSFT > AMZN > NVDA > META > AAPL > GOOGL, and GOOGL sentiment is the weakest since early 2025.

up.why: The MRVL deal is now official (Jefferies desk, 2 Nov), and LITE's FQ2 guide (~$1.6bn vs $1.48bn Street) plus a second NPO/CPO win with >$5bn of commitments add a fundamental leg (Vital Knowledge, 2 Nov). Bloomberg X attention is the top riser in the universe (dz +2.4, 7d return +11% through 30 Oct). LITE sits in the HOT 60-80 band (72), where its own analogs have a negative 5-session median (-0.7%, n=6), so the attention is crowded in the short run. Its BULL 40-60 band (59) has a positive median. Over 1-5 days the stock trades on the 4.5x MRVL ratio; over 2-4 weeks it depends on whether the arb spread or the standalone story dominates.
up.confirm: LITE holds the deal-implied value while MRVL stabilises; buyside sentiment moves above JPM's pre-deal 0 score after the call.
up.weaken: MRVL keeps falling on dilution worries and drags LITE through the fixed ratio, or a shareholder push-back on the ~24% premium.

up.why: UBS's TMI desk (1 Nov) says Friday feedback was far more forgiving than the after-hours move, with Jassy's >40% AWS growth framing for '27/'28 setting up a Street EPS-revision story. UBS ranks it #2 in its Mag 7 order (1 Nov), and GS's specialist lists it among names to revisit (1 Nov). AMZN is HOT 60-80 (64) with a negative 5-session analog median (-1.1%, n=7) but BULL 40-60 (43) with a positive 10-session median (+2.3%). Desk support looks more 2-4 week than 1-5 day; it is still in the hyperscaler de-gross that UBS PB flagged (2 Nov).
up.confirm: Street '27 EPS revisions follow the AWS framing, and AMZN outperforms the other hyperscalers on up-days.
up.weaken: More hyperscaler de-grossing (UBS PB) or financing headlines (the $80bn supplier financing) overwhelm the revision story.

up.why: JPM's specialist (2 Nov) hears NVDA and AVGO as places to hide inside semis because there is 'no more negative discovery value'. UBS ranks NVDA #3 in its Mag 7 order (1 Nov), and BofA's Arya (2 Nov) argues capex discipline extends the cycle with the SOX at a 10% discount to SPX. There is no analog band for NVDA in monitor.json, so this rests on desk evidence alone. It is a relative-safety call for 1-5 days, not a sign that buyers are coming back.
up.confirm: NVDA outperforms SOX on further down-days and into AMD's print.
up.weaken: Funding or credit headlines (S&P on META, AI-debt terms) hit the whole complex regardless of quality.

up.why: GS Research added APH to the US Conviction List with 2027 EBITDA 10% above the Street (GS desk, 2 Nov), and Barclays raised FY27 EPS by 19% and the PT to $111 (Barclays desk, 2 Nov). Bloomberg X attention is rising (dz +1.3, 7d return +7% through 30 Oct). There is no analog band for APH. The broadening trade gives it a 2-4 week tailwind; 1-5 day moves still follow the AI-infra beta.
up.confirm: Further estimate raises and APH holding up on AI down-days (JPM noted APH held up better on Friday).
up.weaken: A renewed AI-infra de-gross that treats APH as a crowded AI long.

up.why: AAPL is the rotation haven: it goes into tonight's print at an all-time-high 36x forward multiple (GS Callahan, 1 Nov), and Bernstein's desk (1 Nov) says conviction in the short has dissipated. The positioning views diverge, though. JPM's survey is -2 (2 Nov), and Barclays (2 Nov) hears plenty of caution, saying the stock trades as the inverse of the semis trade, with memory-driven margin worries into CY27. There is no analog band in monitor.json. The 1-5 day read hinges on the print; over 2-4 weeks, a semis recovery is the main risk to the haven bid.
up.confirm: In-line gross margin and the haven bid hold after the print while semis stay weak.
up.weaken: A gross-margin or iPhone miss, or a semis short-covering rally that pulls money back out of the inverse trade.

down.why: UBS's desk (1 Nov) calls GOOGL the biggest sentiment downtick of the quarter, the most negative since early 2025, on structural AI-Mode search monetization and GCP missing bogeys. GOOGL is last in the UBS Mag 7 order. Bernstein's desk (1 Nov) agrees the feedback is negative but calls it a monetization, not an engagement, problem, and UBS relays SemiAnalysis' GDPx ranking Google's Carbon near the top (2 Nov). GOOG is HOT 60-80 (70) but BULL only 20-40 (29). Its own BULL-band analogs have a positive 5-session median (+2.6%), so washed-out sentiment has tended to mean-revert over 1-5 days, while the search debate is a 2-4 week-plus overhang.
down.confirm: Search-cannibalisation pieces keep coming and GOOGL lags on Tech up-days.
down.weaken: The Carbon launch lands well, or desks start calling GOOGL the contrarian long (Bernstein's view spreading).

down.why: MRVL fell ~13% on Thursday and ~10% on Friday on deal reports (Vital Knowledge, 2 Nov) and helped lead the -7.2% SOX day (JPM, 2 Nov). Redburn (Neutral, 2 Nov) sees dilution and questions for both shareholder bases, and Vital Knowledge raises the JDSU-1999 analogy. On the other side, $1bn+ synergies and year-one accretion could give a small relief rally, and BofA's Arya (2 Nov) stays bullish. There is no analog band for MRVL. Over 1-5 days the stock gets an arb-driven supply overhang; over 2-4 weeks shareholders will be debating the vote.
down.confirm: MRVL keeps underperforming SOX on rebound days as arbitrageurs short it against LITE.
down.weaken: The 8am call convinces on accretion and synergies and MRVL rallies with the Tech bounce.

down.why: INTC is still sliding (-29% on Friday, lower again pre-market per the Jefferies desk, 2 Nov). UBS (1 Nov) reads its supply gap as the start of a supply-constraint theme for the PC and server chain. INTC is HOT 60-80 (69) and BULL 20-40 (21), with negative 5-session analog medians in both bands (-1.2% and -1.3%). GS (1 Nov) has it oversold on 14-day RSI, so a 1-5 day bounce is possible, but the desk tone shows no buyers stepping in.
down.confirm: Further estimate cuts, and AMD or DELL prints confirming PC weakness into 1H27.
down.weaken: An oversold reversal as systematic selling fades this week (UBS, 2 Nov).

down.why: AMD is still crowded: JPM's survey has it at +3, the most long-leaning name this week (2 Nov), and the buyside bar for 2027 DC sits around $80-90bn versus the Street's ~$70bn. Expectations are being trimmed after INTC, though. Barclays (2 Nov) hears a few hundred million taken off the 4Q guide bogey, and Jefferies (2 Nov) relays its EU semis team seeing a lot of good news priced in. AMD is HOT 40-60 (45) and BULL 40-60 (52), with near-flat analog medians. The print on Tuesday decides the 1-5 day move; a 2-4 week de-crowding is the more likely path if the PC drag shows up.
down.confirm: AMD guides around $16.5bn and stays silent on DC 2027, and the stock fades despite a beat.
down.weaken: A high-$16bn guide plus confirmation of 2027 DC growth >100% re-ignites the crowded long.

down.why: Barclays' desk (2 Nov) says QCOM is still a popular short, with strength likely to be faded unless DC delivers real upside. That contrasts with Bernstein's earlier crowding work, which had it as the least crowded semi (ledger, 26 Oct). There is no analog band for QCOM. The print this week is the 1-5 day catalyst.
down.confirm: Soft handset guide and the short pressing further after the print.
down.weaken: A credible DC or AI PC upside surprise forces short covering.

themes.title: De-grossing, not capitulation: systematic selling first, then a squeeze setup
themes.text: Desks agree the October tech flush was a de-gross, not a capitulation. UBS PB (2 Nov) calls last week the 3rd-largest de-gross of the year, concentrated in hyperscalers; its deleveraging indicator triggered, and gross stays elevated because shorts were added. UBS strategy expects ~$100bn of Risk Control selling today before systematic flows fade. Jefferies (1 Nov) had October as its largest net-sell tech month in more than 5 years, with HFs 55% of volume. JPM's Positioning Intel is still only NEUTRAL, and JPM Market Intel is Tactically Bullish on its rebound statistics. Susquehanna's morning note (2 Nov) says HF buying was mostly index short covering, with a 7th week of single-stock net selling. The setup is low net, high gross and heavy shorts, so a sharp squeeze is possible, but no desk is reporting long-only demand.

themes.title: Desk disagreement on AAPL as the AI hedge
themes.text: Bernstein (1 Nov) says AAPL short conviction has faded as it trades as the AI-defensive haven at a record 36x multiple (GS, 1 Nov). JPM's buyside survey (-2) and Barclays' desk (2 Nov) still hear mostly caution and see memory costs as a margin overhang into CY27. Tonight's print tests whether the haven bid outlasts the fundamentals.

themes.title: SemiAnalysis: the 2027 build is locked in; 2028 depends on the governor races
themes.text: SemiAnalysis (1 Nov, forwarded internally by Daniel Grozdea) says ~75% of the 33.8 GW due in 2027 across its top-20 states is already under construction, so the midterms cannot stop 2027. The risk is 2028: 62.2 GW of US net additions, mostly unstarted, sit largely in states electing governors on 3 Nov, and a prolonged Texas permit freeze is the biggest single risk. JPM's specialist (2 Nov) hears that a Democratic sweep is now expected and that data centres may be overstated as a voter issue. GS GIR expects the DC focus to fade after the election (GS Callahan, 1 Nov). All GW figures here are SemiAnalysis facility-pipeline GW and should not be mixed with IT-load GW.

observations.summary: BofA's Arya argues capex cuts would lower peak earnings but extend the cycle through compute scarcity; SOX at 16.4x is a 10% discount to SPX and he stays bullish on NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MRVL, CRDO, LRCX, KLAC, MU, ADI and TXN.
observations.excerpt: if monetizable AI demand remains strong while capacity growth slows, capex cuts could increase compute scarcity and delay rather than pull forward the AI peak
observations.subject: US Semiconductors: AI Capex: Lower Peak, Scarcer Compute, Longer Runway, Higher Multiples - United States

observations.author: Simon Woo
observations.summary: BofA's Simon Woo says Hynix's aggressive DRAM bit-growth and 8-hi HBM4e strategy looks better than Samsung's in a shortage, and raises 2027 DRAM sales +5%.
observations.excerpt: some industry experts believe Hynix’s strategy looks better given shortage (no need for price cuts to sell larger volumes) and NVIDIA’s extra orders for 8-hi HBM4e
